title: Sum
summary: Understand what a sum represents, how addition is written, and how summation notation describes a sequence of terms.

blocks.heading: Overview
blocks.content: A sum is the result obtained by adding two or more quantities. The word can describe the final total, while summation describes the process of adding a collection of terms. Sums appear throughout arithmetic, algebra, calculus, statistics, and many other areas of mathematics.

blocks.heading: Definition
blocks.content: The sum of a finite collection of numbers is the number obtained by combining those numbers using addition.

blocks.heading: Visualising a sum
blocks.alt: One square, plus two squares, plus three squares, equals six squares in total.
blocks.caption: The groups contain 1, 2 and 3 units. Combining all three groups gives a total of 6 units.

blocks.heading: Addition and summation
blocks.content: Addition is the operation of combining quantities. A sum is the result of that operation. Summation is often used when many terms are added, especially when the terms follow a pattern or are described by a sequence.

blocks.heading: Summation notation
blocks.explanation: The Greek capital letter Sigma (Σ) means that the terms are to be added. The index i begins at 1 and increases by 1 until it reaches n. The expression aᵢ represents the term selected at each index.

blocks.heading: Expanding a summation
blocks.explanation: The lower limit tells us to start at i = 1. The upper limit tells us to stop at i = 4. Substituting each integer gives four terms, whose total is 10.

blocks.heading: Sum of the first positive integers
blocks.explanation: This formula gives the sum of the integers from 1 through n. It avoids adding every integer individually.

blocks.heading: Why the formula works
blocks.content: Write the same sum in ascending and descending order. When the two lines are added term by term, every pair has the same value, n + 1. There are n such pairs, so twice the sum is n(n + 1). Dividing by 2 gives the formula.

blocks.heading: Formula derivation
blocks.explanation: Pairing terms from opposite ends produces n pairs, each equal to n + 1.

blocks.heading: Using the formula
blocks.question: Find the sum of the first 10 positive integers.

blocks.heading: Important properties of addition
rows: The order of two addends does not change the sum.
Changing the grouping does not change the sum.
Adding zero leaves a number unchanged.
A number and its additive inverse sum to zero.

blocks.heading: Common points of confusion
blocks.content: A sum is not the same thing as a product: a sum uses addition, while a product uses multiplication. In summation notation, the lower and upper limits identify which terms are included. Always check whether the upper limit is included; in the standard finite notation shown here, it is.

blocks.heading: Try it yourself
blocks.question: Use the formula for the sum of the first n positive integers to find the sum from 1 to 8.
